_README: Group 3 deterministic cross-group continuity package. Start at any link and walk the chain in either direction without asking a Group 3 member to reconstruct history. Every link carries a verification label: VERIFIED (captured output on disk), REPORTED (a named person said so, artifact not held), or GAP (the link genuinely does not exist, with the reason).
_owner: Hemanth Reddy - Cross-Group Observation Continuity & Final Group 3 Handoff Owner

source_state.meaning: SYNTHETIC. This observation was produced deterministically by the Group 3 software path. It is NOT a physical field capture. No Group 3 sensor has produced a recorded reading; available hardware is PRESENT only, per Suraj Surve's ruling of 2026-08-20. This classification must survive every downstream hop unchanged.
source_state.label: VERIFIED

the_observation.identity_rule: Composite: survey_id-zone_id-flight_id-sensor_id-observation_seq. Per Arya Barge's Observation Metadata Contract section 3, identity must not be reduced to the sequence fragment alone. The five component fields are also carried explicitly because Group 1's request body accepts them and Kavy is building zone/flight queryability on them.

provenance.note: provenance_reference is the reviewer-facing pointer to provenance evidence and is DISTINCT from the inline provenance object - ruled by Arya Barge 2026-08-20. Both are required and non-empty.

DEFECT.cause: The V1.2 payload that created this record carried is_synthetic at PACKAGE level; Group 1's API reads it PER OBSERVATION, so it defaulted to false. Proven with a control record sent WITH the flag, which stored true.
DEFECT.why_it_matters: A synthetic observation is recorded in the canonical database as physical. Any downstream consumer reading this record will believe it is real field data.
DEFECT.fix_owner: Raj (Group 1) - a 409 DUPLICATE blocks Group 3 from overwriting it
DEFECT.structurally_prevented_going_forward: V2.2 makes synthetic_state required at OBSERVATION level and forbids laundering SYNTHETIC into PHYSICAL. The defect cannot recur under this contract.

identifiers_reported.event_id: generated at record time - ledger identity, NOT stable across replay
identifiers_reported.execution_id: preserved from the runtime execution - runtime-owned per Karan Barda's 2026-08-14 ruling, therefore varies per execution

governed_abstention.group3_position: Group 3 asks for a deterministic abstention_record_id as the fourth correlation reference, with the ledger event_id retained ALONGSIDE it as the evidence pointer - not instead of it. Reason: an identifier generated at record time cannot correlate a decision across replay. Group 3 has already hit exactly this defect with Group 1's trace_id, which is per-REQUEST rather than per-observation - four calls against this one observation returned four different traces on 2026-08-19.
governed_abstention.derivation_constraint: The deterministic id MUST be derived from stable identity only: observation_id + context_id + ruling. It MUST NOT include execution_id. Karan Barda ruled execution_id runtime-owned on 2026-08-14, so it changes on every execution - including it would make the identifier non-deterministic across replay, which defeats its entire purpose.
governed_abstention.awaiting: Group 4 confirmation of the derivation and the resulting abstention_record_id.

group4_action_input.this_is_a_ruling_not_an_omission: Group 2 ruled GAP: action_eligibility false, abstention_required true. An action_request_id will therefore NEVER exist for this observation, and manufacturing one would be exactly the silent fabrication this handoff exists to prevent. REASON PER THE RULING ARTIFACT (received 2026-08-21): 'Temporal applicability cannot be established because the observation timestamp is unavailable' - source_reference_time null, temporal_relationship UNAVAILABLE. An earlier Group 3 note gave the reason as the observation falling 2 years 8 months outside the 2020-01-01 to 2023-12-31 window; that was Group 3's inference from a message and is NOT what the artifact says. Corrected 2026-08-21. The outcome is unaffected - Group 2's own decision table rules GAP for an out-of-window observation with no adaptation rule too - but the stated reason is disputed, see group2_context.timestamp_discrepancy.
group4_action_input.what_group4_must_produce_instead: A governed abstention record, using the Abstention registry in Karan Barda's own capability map. Group 3 has requested its identifier; it is not yet supplied.
group4_action_input.handoff_envelope: integration/group3_to_group4_handoff.json (TANTRA execution envelope, format confirmed by Karan Barda 2026-08-14)
group4_action_input.handoff_envelope_contract_version: V1.2, NOT V2.2. The envelope is generated from canonical_observation.json, which comes from the V1.2 mission package ingested through Group 1's LOCAL v0.1 schema. The envelope FORMAT is confirmed and current; the observation inside it predates the V2.2 contract. It must be regenerated from a V2.2 observation once Group 1 has aligned its validator and accepted V2.2 live. Stated here rather than left for a reader to discover.

trace_and_correlation.rule: Group 3 does not mint trace IDs - Arya's metadata contract section 15 and Karan Barda's 2026-08-14 ruling that execution_id, trace_id, tenant_id and lineage_hash are runtime-owned.
trace_and_correlation.KNOWN_LIMITATION: Group 1's trace is per-REQUEST, not per-observation. Four calls against this one observation returned four different traces on 2026-08-19, so the trace CANNOT correlate an observation over time. Group 4's runtime separately uses a 16-hex trace-vana- form. The two schemes are unreconciled.
trace_and_correlation.stable_correlation_key: observation_id is the only identifier that is stable across all four groups. Use it, not the trace.
trace_and_correlation.label: VERIFIED
